policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.203: Diaphragmatic/Phrenic Nerve Stimulation
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section I Avery Mark IV / Spirit
source_quote: diaphragmatic/phrenic nerve stimulation with the Mark IV™ Breathing Pacemaker System or the Spirit Diaphragm Pacing Transmitter is medically necessary when all of the following are met: A. Stimulation is used as an alternative to mechanical ventilation for an individual with severe, chronic respiratory failure due to one of the following: 1. Upper cervical spinal cord injury (at or above the C3 vertebral level); 2. Central alveolar hypoventilation disorder;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Diaphragmatic/Phrenic Nerve Stimulation - Avery Mark IV / Spirit System (CPT 64575, 64585, 64590)

criteria.description: Severe chronic respiratory failure due to upper cervical SCI (≥C3) or central alveolar hypoventilation
Intact phrenic nerve, lung, and diaphragm function
Normal chest anatomy and consciousness to participate in rehabilitation

required_documentation: Phrenic nerve conduction study confirming viability
review_notes: Indicated as alternative to mechanical ventilation for upper cervical SCI (≥C3).

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.203: Diaphragmatic/Phrenic Nerve Stimulation
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section II NeuRx RA/4 System
source_quote: diaphragmatic/phrenic nerve stimulation with the NeuRx RA/4 Diaphragm Pacing System® is medically necessary when provided in accordance with the Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE) specifications of the U.S Food and Drug Administration when all of the following are met: A. Stimulation is used as an alternative to mechanical ventilation for an individual with severe, chronic respiratory failure due to one of the following: 1. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS);
clinical_service_or_procedure: NeuRx RA/4 Diaphragm Pacing System® under HDE (CPT 64575, 64585)

criteria.description: Alternative to mechanical ventilation for ALS (age ≥21, FVC ≥45%) OR upper cervical SCI (age ≥18)
Diaphragm movement visible under fluoroscopy or ultrasound
Allows breathing without mechanical ventilator for at least 4 continuous hours/day

review_notes: FDA HDE protocol requirement: ALS requires age ≥21 and FVC ≥45%.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.203: Diaphragmatic/Phrenic Nerve Stimulation
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section III Central Sleep Apnea
source_quote: there is insufficient evidence to support the safety and efficacy of diaphragmatic/phrenic nerve stimulation for any other conditions, including but not limited to, central sleep apnea.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Phrenic Nerve Stimulation for Central Sleep Apnea (Remedé System)

criteria.description: Stimulation requested for central sleep apnea (Remedé System) or unlisted condition

review_notes: Remedé System for CSA is explicitly considered investigational/ unproven.
